_comment: The one place a benchmark number is typed into the site.
Every entry names the artifact it was read from and the path inside that
artifact, and every entry carries a `provenance` field that says exactly
artifact  - the value is a JSON key in a committed harness report. It can
be re-read and diffed by a machine.
prose     - the value appears only in a hand-written report under
benchmarks/. It was recorded by hand from a run whose JSON is
not in the repository. Treat it as weaker evidence even though
That distinction is not pedantry. Four published numbers are prose-only and
one prose figure actually contradicts the artifact beside it; the site says
so rather than presenting all of it at one confidence.
`web/build.py` reads this file and writes only HTML. Nothing here is a live
feed and nothing here is regenerated by a benchmark run, because a benchmark
that silently rewrote the site's claims would be a benchmark that could
To change a number here, change the artifact first and re-read it. If the
artifact and this file disagree, this file is wrong.
conditions: python:3.13, 1 vCPU / 512 MiB / 2048 MiB, command `true`, runtime_requested null
environment: deployed control plane over TLS on 127.0.0.1:18443 with a private CA, single host, one Docker worker (capacity 8) and one Firecracker worker (capacity 4)
statistics_convention: p50/p95/p99 as reported by the harness, so the baseline and the after run are read the same way. The hand-written reports mix `p50_s` and `median_s` for the same runs, which is why a table transcribed from prose can differ from this file in the second decimal.

metrics.label: Run, end to end
metrics.description: Submit to settled record. Matched conditions fingerprint on both sides.
metrics.caveat: The three baseline failures were stale-generation placement errors, so the before side is 22 samples of 25 attempts. The after side succeeded 25/25.

metrics.label: Run, 95th percentile
metrics.description: The tail, which is where a cleanup bug shows up.

metrics.label: Run wall clock, client-observed
metrics.description: The same runs, measured from the client.

metrics.label: Cleanup phase
metrics.description: The phase that was three quarters of the tail.
metrics.caveat: Placement moved only −7.9 % over the same run, so this is a cleanup result and not a placement result.

metrics.label: Placement phase
metrics.description: Reservation plus the machine actually being built.
metrics.caveat: Decomposed on the after side as scheduler 1.946, allocation 0.515, boot 0.534, workspace 0.000. `workspace` is 0 because this workload clones no repository; on a Run that does it is 1.2-1.3 s, which is what the rejected repository cache was aimed at. `placement.*` names are dotted sub-phases of `phase_placement`, so any tool that sums phases must exclude them.

metrics.label: Task phase
metrics.description: The workload itself. Included as a control: it should not change.
metrics.caveat: The command is `true`, so this is process spawn and teardown rather than real work. It is not a workload throughput claim.

metrics.label: Queue wait
metrics.description: Submission to a worker accepting the work.

metrics.label: Client wait no phase claims
metrics.description: The honesty check on the rows above: if the gain had been moved into the unaccounted bucket, this row would have grown.
metrics.caveat: Flat, which is the point: the improvement is inside accounted phases.

metrics.label: Control-plane requests per Run
metrics.description: Accounting delta divided by runs. A cost that should fall when cleanup is fixed.
metrics.caveat: Compared like every other row: the baseline file against the matched after file, both under conditions fingerprint 602f511b90348c50. The block counts HTTP requests to the control plane, not database queries, so it is a transport cost and not a query cost.

metrics.label: Sequential soak
metrics.description: One at a time, censused immediately before and after.
metrics.artifact: benchmarks/after2-soak-sequential-2026-09-30.json → scenarios.soak (succeeded 100, not_succeeded 0, run_total p50 15.1147 / p95 17.806 / p99 19.7436)
metrics.caveat: run_cleanup_failures empty; available vCPUs 12.0 → 12.0; non-terminal sandboxes at the end 0.

metrics.label: Parallel soak
metrics.description: 20 batches of 4. Published as measured, not rounded up.
metrics.artifact: benchmarks/after2-soak-parallel-2026-09-30.json → scenarios.soak (succeeded 77, not_succeeded 3, failed 3, run_total p50 15.592 / p95 20.0437 / p99 23.9289)
metrics.caveat: The three failures are `backend unavailable: transient: no schedulable worker has capacity` at four-way concurrency. Their cause is unattributed and the soak has not been rerun since. The endpoint census returns to baseline, so this is not an accumulation, but the intermediate checkpoints do not: the harness observed up to 3 non-terminal sandboxes and down to 9.0 available vCPUs mid-soak. This is the least flattering number we publish and it is the one on the front page.

metrics.label: Guard gateway CPU, per 64 model requests
metrics.description: Gateway CPU against an identical workload that bypasses it, median of 7 pairs.
metrics.value_label: 0.46 s of gateway CPU, against 0.00 s for the same traffic unguarded
metrics.caveat: 64 requests per sample, concurrency 1, 1 MiB responses, 16 384-byte provider chunks, 2 warmup requests per side, a fresh gateway per pair and alternating order. Local HTTP in a disposable network namespace: not WAN, not TLS, and excluding guest, nftables, watcher and control-plane server. Baseline wall time 0.176 s against 1.614 s guarded. Conventional median only; no confidence interval and no percentile claim.

metrics.label: Guard gateway memory, above idle
metrics.description: Sampled peak RSS minus idle, same 7 pairs.
metrics.value_label: +988 KiB above idle, +1 804 KiB above startup
metrics.caveat: RSS sampled every 5 ms, with VmHWM recorded alongside it.

prose_only.claim: Collecting a 16.8 MiB artifact: 129 360 ms with one read per 64 KiB chunk against 8 945 ms with bounded groups of 32, and 39 ownership calls for a 1 MiB collection because the chunk endpoint brackets every read with two lease checks.
prose_only.why_we_publish_it: It is the mechanism behind the per-Run request-cost row above, and the fix is real and tested.
prose_only.why_it_is_weaker: No JSON artifact for the collection microbenchmark is committed. The numbers exist in benchmarks/AFTER2.md and were recorded by hand.

prose_only.claim: Calibrated in one guest: `git clone --depth 1` moves 8 580 bytes and `git ls-remote -- <url> HEAD` moves 250 950, so the re-check costs 29x the shallow clone.
prose_only.why_we_publish_it: It is the entire argument for turning the repository object cache off, and the OFF/ON rows below are artifact-backed.
prose_only.why_it_is_weaker: The calibration was performed inside the guest during that run and its counters were not committed. The 26x and 29x ratios are arithmetic on these two numbers, so they inherit the weakness.

prose_only.claim: The database held roughly a thousand sandboxes and a thousand Runs during the after run against a nearly empty one at baseline.
prose_only.why_we_publish_it: It establishes that the after measurement was not taken against an empty table.
prose_only.why_it_is_weaker: No artifact records the row counts. The soak report does show the sandbox table reaching 998 rows (970 destroyed, 28 failed) at its end, which is consistent with the claim but is not the same measurement.

known_discrepancies.discrepancy: benchmarks/AFTER2.md records the parallel soak wall clock as 453 s. The soak artifact's 82 observations span 373 s, and the harness records no wall-clock total for the soak scenario.
known_discrepancies.resolution: The site does not publish a parallel soak wall clock. The observation span is not the same quantity as the reported wall clock, so neither number can be asserted without knowing how the hand-written figure was taken.

known_discrepancies.discrepancy: benchmarks/AFTER2.md says "Every checkpoint is the baseline". The artifact shows mid-soak checkpoints reaching 3 non-terminal sandboxes and 9.0 available vCPUs, against 12.0 at both endpoints.
known_discrepancies.resolution: The defensible claim is the one the artifact supports: the census before and the census after are identical, with no new non-terminal sandbox id and no cleanup failure. Mid-soak, a parallel soak of four is expected to hold four sandboxes at once. The site states the endpoint claim only.

known_discrepancies.discrepancy: The hand-written reports quote `median_s` for the after runs and `p50_s` for the baseline runs in the same table, so a figure transcribed from prose can differ from the harness in the second decimal.
known_discrepancies.resolution: This file reads p50 on both sides, which is why run_total before is 25.50 rather than the 25.58 in the prose reports.

rejected.name: Repository object cache
rejected.expected: Less network traffic per Run, because a shared object store replaces a fresh shallow clone.
rejected.measured: 26x more network bytes and about two seconds slower per Run.
rejected.detail: Six OFF runs and seven ON runs against one worker with a pinned commit; every sample asserted a clean checkout, no private mirror left behind, the pinned HEAD, the marker in the captured diff, and a terminal sandbox. Guest receive bytes: 9 280 first and 9 654 median of the rest with the cache off; 260 690 first and 253 223 median of the rest with it on. Placement, median of the warm samples: 6 963 ms off against 9 076 ms on. The cause was measured rather than guessed: `resolve_commit` re-resolves the ref on every Run, including a hit, to re-check that the repository is still anonymously readable, and that one check costs 29x the shallow clone it exists to avoid.
rejected.decision: Off by default, and it stays off. Bounding the re-check by an interval would weaken the property that a repository which has become private stops being served from a shared object store, and that bound is a threat-model decision rather than a performance one.
rejected.found_on_the_way: Two real defects surfaced while measuring it and are fixed with regression tests: the Docker directory listing dropped every subdirectory, and matched only the workspace-relative spelling of entry names while the daemon names copied entries after the directory it was asked for. A recursive walk over a Git mirror therefore stopped after one level and captured no objects at all. The same defect was in `GET /v1/sandboxes/{id}/files`.

not_measured: Network-enabled Firecracker: the worker still lacks the capability to create a TAP device, so microVM Runs are exercised with networking off.
The hosted isolation-provider path was not exercised against a real provider.
The repository object cache on Firecracker and on a hosted runtime.

Any PID-namespace property. No artifact asserts one; the only namespace fact recorded anywhere is Guard's `namespace_isolation` = "fresh user+network namespace; recorded host inode differs; no external interface".
`pressure.observed_at` staleness is accepted and unproven. The admission gate uses `last_heartbeat` freshness, which is the documented contract.
aarch64: cross-build evidence only. No hardware runtime and no performance claim.
Firecracker latency with percentiles: 3 samples, and the harness explicitly withholds p50/p95/p99 below 20 samples.
